title: Identification of a counit cone from an ordinary complementary triangle
statement:
Let $\mathcal T,\mathcal T_Z,\mathcal T_U$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Suppose exact additive functors are supplied with adjunctions $i^*:\mathcal T\rightleftarrows\mathcal T_Z:i_*$, $i_*:\mathcal T_Z\rightleftarrows\mathcal T:i^!$, $j_!:\mathcal T_U\rightleftarrows\mathcal T:j^*$ and $j^*:\mathcal T\rightleftarrows\mathcal T_U:j_*$, where in each displayed pair the left functor is left adjoint (natural Hom bijections, with units and counits satisfying the triangle identities). Suppose $i^*i_*\to1$ and $j^*j_*\to1$ are isomorphisms, $j^*i_*=0$, and for every $M\in\mathcal T$ the ordinary adjunction maps occur in a distinguished triangle $j_!j^*M\to M\to i_*i^*M\to(j_!j^*M)[1]$.

For $K\in\mathcal T$ let $e:i_*i^!K\to K$ be the exceptional counit and $u:K\to j_*j^*K$ the open unit. For any distinguished completion $i_*i^!K\xrightarrow e K\xrightarrow v C\to(i_*i^!K)[1]$, there is a unique map $\beta:C\to j_*j^*K$ satisfying $\beta v=u$, and this map is an isomorphism. Moreover $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(i_*P[m],j_*Q)=0$ for every $P,Q,m$.
